endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A hearing or statement alone does not realize this endpoint unless it yields materially expanded disclosure.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal state in which the city publicly releases materially more stop data or explanatory metadata sufficient to narrow major ambiguity created by suppressed fields.
endpoint_ledger.label: Expanded Data Disclosure

meta.important_question: Will the city disclose materially more stop data beyond the initial partial release, reducing the scope of suppressed unknowns?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Transparency is a core implied terminal question because current public interpretation is constrained by incomplete data.
realization_criteria: Official release adds previously absent categories, disaggregation, or suppression rationale in a way acknowledged by major observers as materially clarifying.
City_oversight_board or city_attorney_office confirms no further routine withholding on the disputed fields within the scenario scope.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Initial release is partial and source text explicitly warns against inventing suppressed facts.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Board visibility alone is not legitimacy repair if public discussion remains dominated by doubts about suppression and process.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal state in which the oversight board is broadly treated as a credible and procedurally legitimate steward of the controversy despite initial incompleteness.
endpoint_ledger.label: Oversight Legitimacy Repair

meta.important_question: Will the oversight board's legitimacy improve or decline after the partial release and public reaction?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly asks to preserve questions of trust and legitimacy.
realization_criteria: Sustained public and elite references characterize the board's handling as credible or fair across at least two distinct channels.
Conflict and distrust directed at the board decline without immediate replacement by new disclosure disputes.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: At T0, legitimacy is mixed: release helps transparency but partiality invites distrust.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Temporary messaging success does not realize the endpoint if institutions still move toward strong transparency or reform action.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal state in which public and institutional discourse primarily accepts the interpretation that incomplete data should not drive major accountability action because safety context is paramount.
endpoint_ledger.label: Safety-and-Context Frame Dominance

meta.important_question: Will the public narrative settle around safety-and-context defenses rather than transparency-and-accountability concerns?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Public safety is one of the named report questions and a central competing interpretation.
realization_criteria: Committee, major media framing, and resident discourse consistently emphasize contextual caution and public safety over disclosure insufficiency.
No major follow-up accountability mechanism is launched beyond symbolic review while safety rhetoric remains central.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: This frame is present but contested at initialization.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Media pressure or activist demands without formal procedural adoption do not realize this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal state in which a competent public body initiates a concrete follow-up process such as a hearing, audit, or official records review beyond the initial release.
endpoint_ledger.label: Formal Follow-Up Oversight

meta.important_question: Will a formal hearing, audit, or equivalent oversight follow-up be initiated by a competent city body?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario implies unresolved oversight process choices after a compelled, partial release.
realization_criteria: City_council_public_safety_committee, city_oversight_board, or another competent authority formally schedules and opens a hearing, audit, or review with stated scope.
The process produces an official agenda, notice, or docket rather than informal calls for action alone.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Follow-up is plausible but not yet initiated at T0 based on source text.
